marketplace.name: 0langas-plugins
marketplace.description: Plugins I build for my own workflow and share publicly.

plugins.name: addonry
plugins.description: Build and test personal Chrome and Firefox extensions.
plugins.author: 0langa
plugins.platforms: Windows is required by the bundled Windows PowerShell launcher. Chrome and Firefox are extension targets, not supported host operating systems.
prerequisites: Chrome or Firefox for the extension being tested
setup: Install the plugin, start a new session, then explicitly invoke Addonry. Its workflow starts only when named or invoked.
Choose Chrome, Firefox, or both. Generated projects and ZIP packages stay local until you request publication.
plugins.example: Use Addonry to build a Chrome and Firefox extension that copies selected links.

plugins.name: computer-custom
plugins.description: Queue Windows desktop actions with a countdown and shared pause controls.
plugins.author: 0langa
plugins.platforms: Windows only. The optional signed UIAccess helper has additional setup requirements.
prerequisites: Optional: the signed UIAccess helper for elevated application windows
setup: Start a new session and explicitly select Computer Custom for prepared batches, shared Snooze, UIAccess, or saved local flows.
Use the bundled Computer tools for ordinary desktop tasks. See the source README for UIAccess setup and input behavior.
plugins.example: Use Computer Custom to prepare a desktop batch with a visible countdown.

plugins.name: recall
plugins.description: Keep project decisions and useful context in a local memory store.
plugins.author: RECALL contributors
plugins.platforms: Python-based local plugin. Platform-specific setup is documented in the source repository; this release does not certify every operating system.
setup: Start a new session in your project and ask RECALL to initialize it.
Memory stays in the project-local .recall store. The plugin supplies its MCP configuration; do not add a second manual server entry.
plugins.example: Use RECALL to remember this project decision and the reasons behind it.

plugins.name: webde-access
plugins.description: Read, organize, draft, and send mail from your WEB.DE account.
plugins.author: 0langa
plugins.platforms: Requires Node.js and an operating-system credential store supported by keytar. Windows is the release-test platform; other platforms may need native dependencies.
prerequisites: A WEB.DE account with IMAP access enabled
An application password when required by your account
setup: Enable IMAP in WEB.DE. Store credentials through the plugin's auth:login helper, following the source README.
Credentials belong in the operating-system credential manager, never in marketplace files or chat. Install dependencies in the plugin directory if the first-start helper requests them.
Ask the plugin to read or draft a message. Sending mail is a separate action that you explicitly request.
plugins.example: Find unread WEB.DE messages from today and draft a reply to the latest one.

plugins.name: agent-handoff
plugins.description: Capture task context and resume it in another coding agent.
plugins.author: 0langa
plugins.platforms: Local Python plugin. The legacy Kimi launcher includes a Windows-specific wrapper.
setup: Install the plugin and start a new session. Ask it to capture or resume a handoff.
Handoff records are stored locally under .handoff. The source repository is public; no private-repository authentication is required.
plugins.example: Create a handoff so I can continue this task in Claude Code.

plugins.name: customization-control
plugins.description: Find duplicate customizations and repair local agent configuration.
plugins.author: 0langa
plugins.platforms: Windows PowerShell helpers and a Python helper for other platforms. Discovery rules may not reflect newer client layouts.
prerequisites: PowerShell on Windows, or Python on macOS/Linux
Local access to the relevant client configuration
setup: Start with a read-only customization audit. Review the proposed changes before applying repairs or deduplication.
Prefer each client's native plugin manager for routine installs and removal. This dormant plugin retains its older cross-provider audit and repair workflows.
plugins.example: Audit my local agent customizations and list duplicates without changing anything.

plugins.name: plugin-evaluation-kimi
plugins.description: Evaluate plugins and skills with static checks and an optional model judge.
plugins.author: PluginEval contributors
plugins.platforms: Python-based local evaluator. Kimi/Moonshot is the default model backend; Codex is an optional backend.
prerequisites: For optional model judging: Kimi API credentials or an authenticated Codex CLI
setup: Use quick-depth static evaluation first; it makes no model calls.
Kimi judging reads PLUGIN_EVAL_KIMI_API_KEY and can consume paid API credits. Select --provider codex for the optional Codex backend, which uses its account allowance.
Review provider and cost settings before requesting model judging or simulations.
plugins.example: Run only the quick static checks on this skill and explain the findings.

plugins.name: plugin-forge
plugins.description: Generate plugin manifests and coordinate releases across coding agents.
plugins.author: 0langa
plugins.platforms: Python-based local authoring tool. Client installation details can drift as host applications change.
setup: Use an existing Forge-managed plugin repository and inspect its status before compiling.
Forge still covers cross-provider authoring and release metadata. Native client plugin managers overlap with its installation functions.
For this marketplace, run its catalog generator after changing the registry; do not hand-edit generated catalogs.
plugins.example: Inspect this Forge-managed plugin and explain any manifest drift.

plugins.name: usage-pulse
plugins.description: View local reports of your coding-agent activity.
plugins.author: 0langa
plugins.platforms: Local Python plugin with host lifecycle hooks. Hook availability varies by client and execution environment.
prerequisites: A local host that supports the bundled hooks
setup: Install the plugin and start a new session. It records local activity counters through host hooks.
Reports read the local Usage Pulse database. It does not store prompt bodies, sync data to a cloud service, or calculate pay-as-you-go charges.
plugins.example: Show my Usage Pulse activity report for today.
